cases.observed: When the automated system tried to download the price-transparency file for Northside Hospital Duluth on 2026-08-19, the server returned an HTTP 403 error, meaning the file could not be retrieved. The grader recorded one occurrence of this barrier, observed at exactly 2026-08-19T16:05:56.736157Z after a single download attempt. Because no verified file could be downloaded, the four remaining dimensions — conformance, completeness, interpretability, and freshness — could not be assessed at all; a machine-readable file (MRF) is the document hospitals are required to post containing their standard charge information. Without a retrievable file, it is impossible to check whether required data fields — such as the median allowed amount, defined as the median of total allowed amounts received from a third-party payer over a period of no less than 12 months and no longer than 15 months — are present and correctly formatted. Similarly, data points such as the 10th percentile allowed amount — the 10th percentile of the total allowed amounts the hospital has historically received from a third party payer — cannot be evaluated without an accessible file.

cases.observed: When the grader tried to download the hospital's machine-readable file (MRF) on 2026-08-19, the server returned an HTTP 409 error, meaning the file could not be retrieved. The specific error message returned was: "HTTP 409: Public access is not permitted on this storage account," which means the file's storage location was configured to block public access at the time of the download attempt. Because no file could be downloaded, the grader was unable to assess whether the file's contents meet any formatting or data requirements; conformance, completeness, interpretability, and freshness were all marked NOT_ASSESSED. Federal regulations require a hospital to make its standard charges publicly available; a file stored in a location that blocks public access cannot satisfy that requirement as written. The grade of F reflects that the file download did not succeed after one attempt; all other dimensions of the file's quality remain unknown until a retrievable file is available for review.

cases.observed: El sistema automatizado intentó descargar el archivo de tarifas (MRF, por sus siglas en inglés: Machine-Readable File) del hospital el 19 de agosto de 2026 y no pudo obtenerlo. El error registrado fue HTTP 409, con el mensaje 'HTTP 409: Public access is not permitted on this storage account', lo que indica que el servidor rechazó la solicitud porque el acceso público al archivo estaba desactivado en el momento de la evaluación. Debido a que no se pudo descargar ni verificar ningún archivo, las dimensiones de conformidad, integridad, interpretabilidad y actualidad no pudieron evaluarse en esta ocasión. La regulación federal establece que los hospitales deben poner a disposición del público su lista de cargos estándar; un archivo que no puede descargarse públicamente no cumple con esa condición de acceso. Cuando CMS determina que existe un incumplimiento material, puede solicitar al hospital que presente un plan de acción correctiva mediante una notificación formal de infracción.
